sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·罗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 甚至早在黑胶唱片时代我在夜总会打碟的时候，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 每晚你都要带着300件你最珍贵的传家宝去上班，你把DJ台变成了一个美丽的、有50年历史的手工艺品的活体快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在即可在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today, there's no knock on the door, just the sound of the SWAT team smashing through it.
sentences.zh: 今天，没有人在门口敲门，只有特警队破门而入的声音。

sentences.en: And it's happening all over the country.
sentences.zh: 而且这种情况正在全国各地发生。

sentences.en: A year-long investigation by The Times reveals a police tactic that has led to dozens of avoidable deaths, gruesome injuries, and costly legal settlements.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》历时一年的调查揭露了一种警方战术，该战术已导致数十起可以避免的死亡、骇人的受伤以及代价高昂的法律和解。

sentences.en: It's Monday, March 20th.
sentences.zh: 今天是3月20日，星期一。

sentences.en: Kevin, can you tell me the story of Hank McGee?
sentences.zh: 凯文，你能给我讲讲汉克·麦基的故事吗？

sentences.en: Hank McGee is a 28-year-old who lives in Burleson County, Texas.
sentences.zh: 汉克·麦基是一名28岁的年轻人，住在德克萨斯州伯勒森县。

sentences.en: It's in central Texas.
sentences.zh: 它位于德克萨斯州中部。

sentences.en: Kind of a dusty place.
sentences.zh: 是个有点尘土飞扬的地方。

sentences.en: Kevin Sack is an investigative reporter based in Atlanta.
sentences.zh: 凯文·萨克是一名常驻亚特兰大的调查记者。

sentences.en: In December of 2013, a friend of his became a confidential informant.
sentences.zh: 2013年12月，他的一个朋友成了一名秘密线人。

sentences.en: He was a guy that went to jail for probation violation.
sentences.zh: 他是一个因违反缓刑规定而入狱的家伙。

sentences.en: He was a meth addict.
sentences.zh: 他是个瘾君子。

sentences.en: One day, he calls in the sheriff's investigator who had arrested him.
sentences.zh: 有一天，他打电话给逮捕他的治安官调查员。

sentences.en: Gene, you said you wanted to eradicate the problem.
sentences.zh: 吉恩，你说过你想彻底根除这个问题。

sentences.en: And I've been thinking for the past couple of days that maybe I'm put in this position to help you do this.
sentences.zh: 我过去几天一直在想，也许我被安排在这个位置上是为了帮你们做到这一点。

sentences.en: And says that he's got some information for him.
sentences.zh: 并说他有一些关于他的情报。

sentences.en: I know it's an illegal girl operation.
sentences.zh: 我知道这是一场非法的制毒行动。

sentences.en: And he tells him that Hank McGee is growing marijuana hydroponically.
sentences.zh: 他告诉他，汉克·麦基正在水培大麻。

sentences.en: Make it real small, really?
sentences.zh: 弄得很小，真的吗？

sentences.en: It's kind of small.
sentences.zh: 有点小。

sentences.en: It's good.
sentences.zh: 挺好的。

sentences.en: But that ain't the point.
sentences.zh: 但重点不是这个。

sentences.en: It's illegal.
sentences.zh: 这是违法的。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Weapons are involved.
sentences.zh: 涉及武器。

sentences.en: AR-15s.
sentences.zh: AR-15步枪。

sentences.en: AR-30s.
sentences.zh: AR-30步枪。

sentences.en: In his mobile home, in his trailer.
sentences.zh: 在他的移动房屋里，在他的拖车里。

sentences.en: I mean, the boy's ready for war.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这小子已经准备好打仗了。

sentences.en: With who, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 跟谁打，我不知道。

sentences.en: But I'm just giving you that information.
sentences.zh: 但我只是把这个情报提供给你。

sentences.en: Because if the boy does grab a hold of a gun, try not to shoot him.
sentences.zh: 因为如果这小子真的抓起一把枪，尽量别开枪打他。

sentences.en: Eventually, this turns into an investigation that really consisted of little more than driving by the trailer and taking some photographs.
sentences.zh: 最终，这演变成了一项调查，其实也就是开车经过拖车拍几张照片而已。

sentences.en: The deputies were able to go to a local magistrate and obtain a search warrant.
sentences.zh: 警员们得以去当地治安法官那里获得搜查令。

sentences.en: Then what happened?
sentences.zh: 后来发生了什么？

sentences.en: Dark one night, a force of Burleson County deputies, their version of a SWAT team, descends upon this trailer.
sentences.zh: 一天深夜，一群伯勒森县的警员，也就是他们那里的特警队，包围了这个拖车。

sentences.en: They roll across a cattle guard and down a dirt road.
sentences.zh: 他们碾过一个护牛栏，沿着一条土路驶去。

sentences.en: It's pitch black.
sentences.zh: 里面漆黑一片。

sentences.en: And Hank is inside sleeping with his pregnant girlfriend.
sentences.zh: 汉克正和怀孕的女友在里面睡觉。

sentences.en: The only light inside the trailer was from the bulbs on a Christmas tree.
sentences.zh: 拖车里唯一的亮光来自圣诞树上的灯泡。

sentences.en: They had first set off a flashbang grenade, which is a stun device that emits this intense blast of sound and light that's designed to sort of incapacitate a suspect.
sentences.zh: 他们首先引爆了一枚眩晕弹，这是一种眩晕装置，会发出强烈的声响和闪光，旨在使嫌疑人暂时丧失行动能力。

sentences.en: But they had gotten some directions confused, directions given by the confidential informant.
sentences.zh: 但他们搞混了一些方向，那是秘密线人给的方向。

sentences.en: They thought the bedroom was on the left when, in fact, it was on the right.
sentences.zh: 他们以为卧室在左边，事实上却在右边。

sentences.en: And that's where they set the flashbang off, was just outside that window.
sentences.zh: 而他们引爆眩晕弹的地方，就在那扇窗户外。

sentences.en: As a result, it really did not incapacitate Hank.
sentences.zh: 结果，它并没有真正让汉克失去行动能力。

sentences.en: And what woke them up was the banging on the door with the battering ram that came immediately after that.
sentences.zh: 叫醒他们的是随之而来的用破门锤砸门的声音。

sentences.en: Hank starts calling out, who is it?
sentences.zh: 汉克开始大喊，是谁？

sentences.en: Who is it?
sentences.zh: 是谁？

sentences.en: Who's there?
sentences.zh: 是谁在那儿？

sentences.en: They get no answer.
sentences.zh: 他们没有得到任何回答。

sentences.en: As the banging on the door continues, he runs into his bedroom and grabs a rifle out of a closet.
sentences.zh: 随着砸门声继续，他跑进卧室，从衣柜里抓出一支步枪。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Comes out of the bedroom.
sentences.zh: 走出卧室。

sentences.en: And just as the door bursts open, he raises the rifle and he starts firing.
sentences.zh: 就在门被撞开的一瞬间，他举起步枪开始射击。

sentences.en: Only after he fires does he hear the deputies outside screaming, sheriff's department, search warrant.
sentences.zh: 直到开枪后，他才听到外面警员的尖叫声：治安官部门，搜查令。

sentences.en: He immediately drops the gun.
sentences.zh: 他立刻扔下枪。

sentences.en: And as they get to the door, they walk over the prone body of a sheriff's deputy, Adam Soders, who, despite wearing a bulletproof vest, has been struck in the head and killed.
sentences.zh: 当他们冲到门口时，他们跨过了治安官警员亚当·索德斯的俯卧尸体，他尽管穿着防弹衣，但头部中弹身亡。

sentences.en: Terrible.
sentences.zh: 太可怕了。

sentences.en: So he died pretty much instantly?
sentences.zh: 所以他几乎是瞬间死亡的？

sentences.en: Instantly.
sentences.zh: 瞬间死亡。

sentences.en: Central Texas lawmen killed in the line of duty.
sentences.zh: 德州中部执法人员在执行公务时殉职。

sentences.en: New details tonight.
sentences.zh: 今晚的新细节。

sentences.en: Sergeant Adam Soders with the Burleson County Sheriff's Office was shot and killed early this morning.
sentences.zh: 伯勒森县治安官办公室的警长亚当·索德斯今天凌晨遭枪击身亡。

sentences.en: 28-year-old Henry McGee of Somerville is in the Brenham City Jail charged with capital murder of a police officer.
sentences.zh: 来自萨默维尔的28岁亨利·麦基被关押在布伦纳姆市监狱，被控谋杀警官。

sentences.en: His attorney says the shooting was an accident, claiming he didn't know it was the deputies entering his rural home.
sentences.zh: 他的律师称这起枪击事件是一场意外，声称他不知道进入他乡村住宅的是警员。

sentences.en: He thought it was a burglar.
sentences.zh: 他以为那是江洋大盗。

sentences.en: Kevin, my sense of how police work is done, and in all the television shows I watched growing up of how police work is done, they announced themselves.
sentences.zh: 凯文，根据我对警察工作方式的理解，以及我从小看过的所有关于警察工作的电视节目，他们都是会先表明身份的。

sentences.en: So what are we talking about here?
sentences.zh: 那我们现在在谈论什么？

sentences.en: What are we seeing?
sentences.zh: 我们看到了什么？

sentences.en: So there's a special breed of warrant, unlike the others, unlike the ones that we've seen on TV.
sentences.zh: 所以有一种特殊类别的搜查令，不同于其他的，不同于我们在电视上看到的那些。

sentences.en: This warrant, it's called a no-knock warrant.
sentences.zh: 这种搜查令被称为“不敲门搜查令”。

sentences.en: And it's called that, obviously, enough, I guess, because the police don't have to knock.
sentences.zh: 我想，顾名思义，它之所以叫这个名字，是因为警察不需要敲门。

sentences.en: They don't have to announce themselves before entering a house.
sentences.zh: 他们在进入房屋之前不需要表明身份。

sentences.en: And a lot of people, I think, are surprised to learn this exists.
sentences.zh: 我想很多人得知这一点都会感到惊讶。

sentences.en: I had no idea that such a thing existed.
sentences.zh: 我根本不知道还有这种东西。

sentences.en: It's pervasive.
sentences.zh: 它无处不在。

sentences.en: The problem is we don't really know how pervasive because there are no federal requirements that police departments report on SWAT activities.
sentences.zh: 问题是我们并不知道它有多普遍，因为没有联邦要求警察局报告特警队的行动。

sentences.en: How often have you found that these no-knock warrants are being used by SWAT teams around the United States?
sentences.zh: 你发现美国各地的特警队使用这种不敲门搜查令的频率有多高？

sentences.en: Thousands of times a year, clearly.
sentences.zh: 显然一年有数千次。

sentences.en: And it's not uncommon that they go badly.
sentences.zh: 而且它们搞砸了也并非不常见。

sentences.en: In all the no-knock raids that you've investigated, how many people have died?
sentences.zh: 在你调查的所有不敲门突袭中，有多少人死亡？

sentences.en: We came up with a total of 94 deaths between 2010 and 2016.
sentences.zh: 我们统计出2010年至2016年间共有94人死亡。

sentences.en: That's clearly a minimum.
sentences.zh: 这显然是个最低数字。

sentences.en: Those are the ones that we could find out about.
sentences.zh: 这些只是我们能够查到的。

sentences.en: And of that 94, 81 were civilians and 13 were police officers.
sentences.zh: 在这94人中，81人是平民，13人是警察。

sentences.en: Can you tell me how it is that a no-knock warrant is legal?
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我为什么不敲门搜查令是合法的吗？

sentences.en: It would seem to me that if I'm in my apartment and the cops rush through the door, that I would have some legal protection.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，如果我在自己的公寓里，警察冲进门来，我应该享有某种法律保护才对。

sentences.en: How does that work?
sentences.zh: 这到底是怎么运作的？

sentences.en: Well, you would think so because going all the way back to the early 1600s, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，你本来会这么认为，因为一直追溯到17世纪初，对吧？

sentences.en: We've had the Castle Doctrine and English Common Law, which gives residents protection against invasions without announcement by the king's officers.
sentences.zh: 我们有城堡防卫权和英国普通法，它为居民提供保护，防止国王的官员在没有事先通报的情况下进行侵入。

sentences.en: It goes that far back.
sentences.zh: 它可以追溯到那么久以前。

sentences.en: It goes that far back.
sentences.zh: 它可以追溯到那么久以前。

sentences.en: And that was enshrined in the Fourth Amendment to our Constitution in, I believe, 1791.
sentences.zh: 而且这一原则被写入了我们宪法的第四修正案，我相信是在1791年。

sentences.en: No unreasonable searches and seizures.
sentences.zh: 即免受无理搜查和扣押。

sentences.en: But over the years, the Supreme Court has rolled all of that back.
sentences.zh: 但多年来，最高法院已经将所有这些都推翻了。

sentences.en: After a series of rulings over the last 20 or 30 years,
sentences.zh: 在过去20到30年的一系列裁决之后，

sentences.en: the situation is now that there's explicit authority for officers to go in without knocking or announcing when there's a risk of danger or a risk of evidence destruction.
sentences.zh: 现在的状况是，当存在危险风险或毁灭证据的风险时，有明确的授权允许警官在不敲门或不通报的情况下进入。

sentences.en: So that's the right of the police to execute a warrant.
sentences.zh: 所以这是警察执行搜查令的权力。

sentences.en: But then there's this fundamental right of the citizen to self-defense in his or her home.
sentences.zh: 但随后还有公民在其家园中进行自卫的基本权利。

sentences.en: How has that tension played out in the courts?
sentences.zh: 这种紧张关系在法庭上是如何体现的？

sentences.en: It really comes down to what the shooter knew, what the shooter perceived at the time he was shooting.
sentences.zh: 这实际上归结为开枪者在开枪时知道什么，感知到什么。

sentences.en: In cases where the shooter can demonstrate that they really did not know who they were shooting at and that they felt that they were firing at self-defense,
sentences.zh: 在开枪者能够证明他们确实不知道自己向谁开枪，并且他们觉得自己在进行自卫的情况下，

sentences.en: then I think that grand juries and juries and prosecutors have been sympathetic.
sentences.zh: 那么我认为大陪审团、陪审团和检察官都是同情的。

sentences.en: So what happened to Hank McGee?
sentences.zh: 那么汉克·麦基怎么样了？

sentences.en: Hank McGee spends a month or two in jail and a grand jury that's been impaneled in Burleson County is given his case.
sentences.zh: 汉克·麦基在监狱里呆了一两个月，伯勒森县组建的一个大陪审团接手了他的案子。

sentences.en: They hear from the officers that were involved that day.
sentences.zh: 他们听取了那天参与其中的警员的陈述。

sentences.en: They also hear from his girlfriend who was able to give Hank's side of the story that they had no idea who it was barging in and they thought they were being robbed and he fired in order to protect himself and his girlfriend.
sentences.zh: 他们还听取了他女友的陈述，女友能够说出汉克方面的故事：他们根本不知道是谁闯进来的，他们以为自己遭遇了抢劫，他开枪是为了保护自己和女友。

sentences.en: And that grand jury chose, perhaps surprisingly, not to indict McGee for capital murder.
sentences.zh: 而那个大陪审团，也许出人意料地，选择不以谋杀罪起诉麦基。

sentences.en: You know, you kill a police officer, it's capital murder, and the potential punishment is the death penalty.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你杀死了一名警官，这就是谋杀，潜在的惩罚是死刑。

sentences.en: It's a very serious business.
sentences.zh: 这是一件非常严重的事情。

sentences.en: He was indicted by this grand jury for drug possession, and his case actually goes to trial on April 3rd.
sentences.zh: 他被这个大陪审团以藏毒罪起诉，他的案子实际上在4月3日开庭审理。

sentences.en: We've been talking about cases where people with criminal ties or suspected criminal ties are targeted by police.
sentences.zh: 我们一直在讨论有犯罪联系或涉嫌犯罪联系的人被警察盯上的案件。

sentences.en: Are innocent people ever caught up in these raids?
sentences.zh: 无辜的人曾经卷入这些突袭中吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 当然有。

sentences.en: And I would never contend that it's the majority of the time, but there have certainly been instances where total innocence have been caught in the crossfire.
sentences.zh: 我绝不会认为这是绝大多数情况，但确实存在完全无辜的人被卷入交火的实例。

sentences.en: I'm Shaites, mayor of the town of Berwyn Heights, Maryland, from 2004 to 2015.
sentences.zh: 我是夏伊茨，2004年至2015年马里兰州伯温海茨镇的镇长。

sentences.en: I had returned home from my day job with the goal of just walking my dogs and hurrying off to a community meeting that I was hosting that evening.
sentences.zh: 我结束了白天的工作回到家，目的是遛遛狗，然后赶紧去参加我那天晚上主持的一个社区会议。

sentences.en: When I got back from walking my dogs, there was a package on my doorstep.
sentences.zh: 当我遛完狗回来时，门廊上有一个包裹。

sentences.en: And I brought it in, left it unopened on a living room table, and went upstairs into my room to change.
sentences.zh: 我把它拿进来，没拆封就放在起居室的桌子上，然后上楼去我的房间换衣服。

sentences.en: When my mother-in-law, who lived with us at the time, yelled out something that didn't make any sense.
sentences.zh: 当时和我住在一起的岳母大喊了一些莫名其妙的话。

sentences.en: I heard the word SWAT.
sentences.zh: 我听到了“特警”这个词。

sentences.en: I walked over to the window, looked out the window to see there.
sentences.zh: 我走到窗前，向外望去。

sentences.en: It was, you know, middle of summer, so broad daylight.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那是盛夏，所以正是大白天。

sentences.en: When I heard the sound of an explosion, which was the sound of a battering ram blowing in our front door.
sentences.zh: 当我听到一声爆炸声时，那是破门锤撞开我们前门的声音。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Followed by immediate gunfire.
sentences.zh: 紧接着是密集的枪声。

sentences.en: It was, you know, terrifying.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这太可怕了。

sentences.en: I hit the ground.
sentences.zh: 我扑倒在地。

sentences.en: I, you know, heard boots running, more gunfire.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我听到靴子奔跑的声音，还有更多的枪声。

sentences.en: After initially hearing boots run down into my basement, I heard people saying, upstairs, upstairs, which is where I was.
sentences.zh: 在最初听到靴子跑进我的地下室后，我听到有人在喊：楼上，楼上，也就是我所在的地方。

sentences.en: And I yelled out, please, I'm up here.
sentences.zh: 我大喊道：求求你们，我在上面。

sentences.en: Don't shoot.
sentences.zh: 别开枪。

sentences.en: They told me to come to the landing where they could see me.
sentences.zh: 他们叫我走到他们能看见我的平台上。

sentences.en: I was in my boxer shorts barefoot.
sentences.zh: 我穿着平角短裤，赤脚。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Because I was midway through getting dressed.
sentences.zh: 因为我衣服穿到了一半。

sentences.en: I, when I was told to put my hands above my head and walk down the stairs, and I could see, you know, two rifles kind of pointed at me.
sentences.zh: 我，当我被告知把双手举过头顶走下楼梯时，我能看到，你知道，有两支步枪正对着我。

sentences.en: So when I got to the bottom of the steps, men grabbed me.
sentences.zh: 所以当我走到台阶底部时，几个男人抓住了我。

sentences.en: They held my hands behind my back.
sentences.zh: 他们把我的双手反剪在背后。

sentences.en: They put on those plastic cuffs.
